subject: How to Define Regularizing Laplace Priors in Multi-level Models?

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: How to Define Regularizing Laplace Priors in Multi-level Models?
parts:
Say one would like to model something using a basic model:
Y[n]~ Dist(Link(theta[n]))

theta[n] <- alpha + X[n]*beta
where alpha is an intercept, X a row vector of predictors, and beta a vector of parameters.

But if X is long and we only expect a small number of effects, we can use regularizing priors:
beta ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)

But... if we have multi-level structure things start to look weird to me:
Y[n]~ Dist(Link(theta[n]))

theta[n] <- alpha + X[n]*beta[cluster[n]]

beta[c] <- MuBeta + DeltaBeta[c];

MuBeta ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)

DeltaBeta[c] ~ Normal(zeros, SigmaDeltaBeta)

SigmaDeltaBeta ~ HalfCauchy(0,1)

Which seems not quite right to me...

I think I'd like to be able to do something like:
(MuBeta + DeltaBeta[c]) ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)

instead of defining the double exp prior only over MuBeta...

1) Can I do this in Stan?
2a) Do I need to do some Jacobian adjustment if I do?
2b) If so, how do I figure out what the adjustment should be?
3) Most importantly, is there a better way to implement the kind of model I am suggesting here?

Thanks ahead of time!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to Define Regularizing Laplace Priors in Multi-level Models?
parts:
> On May 25, 2015, at 2:32 PM, Cody Ross <ctr...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
>
> Say one would like to model something using a basic model:
> Y[n]~ Dist(Link(theta[n]))
>
> theta[n] <- alpha + X[n]*beta
> where alpha is an intercept, X a row vector of predictors, and beta a vector of parameters.
>
> But if X is long and we only expect a small number of effects, we can use regularizing priors:
> beta ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)

Just to be clear here --- Stan's not going to drive parameter
estimates to zero, but it may be close in either optimization or
sampling.

> But... if we have multi-level structure things start to look weird to me:
> Y[n]~ Dist(Link(theta[n]))
>
> theta[n] <- alpha + X[n]*beta[cluster[n]]
>
> beta[c] <- MuBeta + DeltaBeta[c];
>
> MuBeta ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)
>
> DeltaBeta[c] ~ Normal(zeros, SigmaDeltaBeta)
>
> SigmaDeltaBeta ~ HalfCauchy(0,1)
>
> Which seems not quite right to me...

Looks OK to me.

The more usual way to write all this would be:

beta ~ normal(mu_beta, sigma_beta);

mu_beta ~ double_exponential(0, 0.5);

But it's more efficient in the non-centered parameterization:

beta_raw ~ normal(0, 1);

beta <- mu_beta + sigma_beta * beta_raw;

> I think I'd like to be able to do something like:
> (MuBeta + DeltaBeta[c]) ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)

This looks wrong --- if you put that in a loop, you'll be
giving a prior to MuBeta multiple times.

> instead of defining the double exp prior only over MuBeta...
>
> 1) Can I do this in Stan?
> 2a) Do I need to do some Jacobian adjustment if I do?
> 2b) If so, how do I figure out what the adjustment should be?
> 3) Most importantly, is there a better way to implement the kind of model I am suggesting here?
>

Maybe just an easier way to think about it --- see above.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to Define Regularizing Laplace Priors in Multi-level Models?
parts:
If we can run to 15 decimal places of accuracy and get underflow working
in our favor, perhaps. Otherwise, the gradient-based method suffers from
finite steps sizes never hitting zero exactly. There are specialized
optimizers to deal with the truncation implicit in the step size for
double exponential (aka Laplace, or L1) regularization.

- Bob

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: Re: How to Define Regularizing Laplace Priors in Multi-level Models?
parts:
I don't like the way the first model I wrote looks, because (it seems to me), Beta does not actually have double exponential priors on its elements. MuBeta does, but I am not sure how effective this model parametrization would be if there is a lot of heterogeneity in which of the Beta parameters are important in each cluster.

So perhaps, a better way to ask the questions, is there any way to write the model so that Beta[c] actually has double exponential priors on its elements, while still sharing information across clusters?

It look hacky, but  could I run what I wrote before:
for(c in 1:cluster)
(MuBeta + DeltaBeta[c]) ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)
and then run some secondary adjustment to lp__ than 'undoes' the effect on MuBeta having been given multiple priors?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to Define Regularizing Laplace Priors in Multi-level Models?
parts:
> On May 26, 2015, at 4:33 PM, Cody Ross <ctr...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
>
> I don't like the way the first model I wrote looks, because (it seems to me), Beta does not actually have double exponential priors on its elements. MuBeta does, but I am not sure how effective this model parametrization would be if there is a lot of heterogeneity in which of the Beta parameters are important in each cluster.
>
> So perhaps, a better way to ask the questions, is there any way to write the model so that Beta[c] actually has double exponential priors on its elements, while still sharing information across clusters?

> It look hacky, but could I run what I wrote before:
> for(c in 1:cluster)
> (MuBeta + DeltaBeta[c]) ~ DoubleExponential(0, 0.5)
>
> and then run some secondary adjustment to lp__ than 'undoes' the effect on MuBeta having been given multiple priors?

I wouldn't recommend that. You want the hierarchical prior to
shrink to "no different from population mean" not to zero. That is,
the hierarchical prior controls shrinkage on the difference from the
population means and thus controls the variability in the population.

- Bob

I will say that it can make sense to use different priors for Bayesian posterior mode estimation than for full Bayes. This is discussed in these two papers:
http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/chung_cov_matrices.pdf
http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/chung_etal_Pmetrika2013.pdf
